items.clue: Looks like a white version of broccoli: a tight head of creamy curds wrapped in green leaves.
items.alt: Riced or mashed as a low-carb substitute, or roasted with cheese; it also comes in orange and purple varieties.

items.name: green bean
items.description: A long thin green pod eaten whole, snapped and cooked
items.clue: Long, thin, crisp pods eaten whole, often snapped at the ends before cooking.
items.alt: Baked in a casserole topped with crispy onions at holiday dinners; also called string or snap pods.

items.name: sweet potato
items.description: A sweet orange-fleshed root tuber with reddish skin, baked or mashed
items.clue: An elongated tuber with reddish skin and bright orange flesh, often baked or mashed.
items.alt: Roasted into wedges or topped with marshmallows in a holiday casserole; often mistakenly called a yam.

items.name: eggplant
items.description: A large glossy dark purple vegetable with spongy flesh, also called aubergine
items.clue: Large and glossy with deep purple skin and spongy pale flesh, used in moussaka and parmigiana.
items.alt: Also called aubergine; it soaks up oil when cooked and is the base of baba ganoush.

items.name: zucchini
items.description: A long green summer squash, cucumber-shaped, usually cooked
items.clue: A long, smooth, dark green summer squash, often sliced and grilled.
items.alt: Also called courgette; gardeners end up with far too many, so it gets baked into loaves and spiralised into noodles.

items.name: asparagus
items.description: Thin green spear-shaped shoots with pointed tips, steamed or grilled
items.clue: Thin green spears with pointed tips, steamed or grilled in spring.
items.alt: Famous for making your pee smell odd after eating it; the woody ends are snapped off before cooking.

items.name: radish
items.description: A small round red-skinned root with white peppery crunchy flesh
items.clue: A small, round, bright red-pink root with white flesh and a peppery bite.
items.alt: Sliced thin into salads for crunch; it grows very fast, and some long white varieties are used in Asian cooking.

items.name: beet
items.description: A round dark red-purple root vegetable that stains, earthy and sweet
items.clue: A round, deep purple-red root that stains your hands and cutting board.
items.alt: Roasted, pickled or made into borscht soup; one pale variety is processed into table sugar.

items.name: brussels sprout
items.description: A tiny green cabbage-like bud growing in rows on a tall stalk
items.clue: Looks like a tiny cabbage, green and round, and many kids hate its bitter taste.
items.alt: Grows in rows up a tall, thick stalk and is a traditional side at holiday roast dinners.

items.name: kale
items.description: A tough dark green leafy cabbage with curly ruffled leaves
items.clue: Dark, curly, tough green leaves, trendy as a superfood and baked into crispy chips.
items.alt: A hardy leafy green that survives frost; it's massaged with oil for salads or blended into green smoothies.

items.name: artichoke
items.description: A green thistle bud with tough scaly leaves and a tender heart
items.clue: A globe of thick, overlapping, spiky green leaves; you scrape the soft base of each leaf with your teeth.
items.alt: The edible part is the bud of a thistle; its tender heart is marinated or made into a creamy dip with spinach.

items.name: chili pepper
items.description: A small hot spicy pepper, red or green, that burns the mouth
items.clue: Small, red or green and very hot; it can make your mouth burn and your eyes water.
items.alt: Its heat is measured in Scoville units; jalapenos and habaneros are kinds of it.

items.name: turnip
items.description: A round white root vegetable with purple top, mildly bitter
items.clue: A round root with white skin and a purple top, mashed or roasted in winter.
items.alt: A humble, slightly peppery root that was once carved into lanterns before pumpkins were used.

items.name: rhubarb
items.description: Long red sour stalks with big poisonous leaves, cooked in pies
items.clue: Long, sour, pinkish-red stalks with huge poisonous leaves, cooked into pies and crumbles.
items.alt: Very tart, it's usually stewed with lots of sugar and often paired with strawberries.

items.name: okra
items.description: A green ridged pointed pod with slimy seeds, used in gumbo
items.clue: Green, finger-shaped, ridged pods that turn slimy when cooked, used in gumbo.
items.alt: Sometimes called lady's fingers; it's popular breaded and cooked crisp in the American South and in Indian curries.

items.name: peanut
items.description: A legume seed in a crinkly beige shell that grows underground
items.clue: Grows underground in a papery, crinkly shell holding two kernels; sold roasted and salted at ballgames.
items.alt: A legume rather than a true tree kernel, it's a common serious allergy and is ground into a sandwich spread.

items.name: almond
items.description: A flat oval pale brown nut with pointed tip from an almond tree
items.clue: A teardrop-shaped kernel with brown skin grown on orchard trees; made into marzipan and dairy-free milk.
items.alt: Flat, oval and crunchy, often sliced onto desserts; it comes from a close relative of the peach.

items.name: walnut
items.description: A wrinkly brain-shaped nut in a hard round shell
items.clue: A wrinkly kernel that looks like a tiny brain, inside a hard round shell.
items.alt: Chopped into brownies and banana loaf; its dark, heavy timber is prized for furniture.

items.name: cashew
items.description: A curved kidney-shaped pale nut grown from a tropical cashew apple
items.clue: Curved and creamy, it grows hanging below a fleshy tropical 'apple'.
items.alt: Always sold shelled because the shell contains an irritating oil; blended into creamy vegan sauces.

items.name: pecan
items.description: A smooth oval brown-shelled nut, used in pecan pie
items.clue: A smooth, oblong brown shell with a sweet, buttery kernel, baked into a famous Southern pie.
items.alt: Grows on big hickory-family trees in the southern US and is candied into pralines.

items.name: pistachio
items.description: A small green nut in a cream shell that splits open
items.clue: A small green kernel inside a beige shell that splits partly open on its own.
items.alt: Gives a pale green colour to ice cream and baklava; you crack the half-open shells with your fingers.

items.name: hazelnut
items.description: A small round brown nut with smooth shell, used in chocolate spreads
items.clue: Small, round and brown; the key ingredient in a famous chocolate spread.
items.alt: Also called a filbert, it grows on bushy shrubs and is a popular coffee syrup flavour.

items.name: acorn
items.description: The small nut of an oak tree with a scaly cap, eaten by squirrels
items.clue: Small, with a little cap on top; it falls from oaks and squirrels bury it for winter.
items.alt: A proverb says mighty giants grow from these little things; it's egg-shaped and sits in a scaly cup.

items.name: chestnut
items.description: A glossy brown nut in a spiky husk, roasted over fire
items.clue: Glossy brown, inside a spiky green husk; roasted on an open fire in winter.
items.alt: Sold hot from street carts in cold weather; its sweet, floury meat is made into stuffing and puree.

items.name: rice
items.description: Small white or brown grains grown in flooded paddies, boiled and eaten
items.clue: Tiny white or brown kernels that are boiled or steamed; a staple for billions of people in Asia.
items.alt: Grown in flooded paddy fields; it's rolled into sushi and stirred into risotto.

items.name: wheat
items.description: A golden cereal grass whose grains are ground into flour for bread
items.clue: A golden cereal crop whose kernels are ground into flour for bread.
items.alt: Waves in vast amber fields across the prairies and contains gluten.

items.name: oat
items.description: A cereal grain rolled into flakes for porridge and fed to horses
items.clue: A cereal crop whose rolled flakes are cooked into porridge for breakfast.
items.alt: Horses love it, and it's baked into chewy cookies and granola bars.

items.name: barley
items.description: A cereal grain with long bristles, used in soup and brewing beer
items.clue: A cereal crop with long bristly whiskers, malted to brew beer and whisky.
items.alt: Pearled kernels of it go into hearty beef soups; it's one of the first crops ever farmed.

items.name: quinoa
items.description: Tiny round seeds from the Andes, cooked like a grain, high protein
items.clue: Tiny round seeds that cook up fluffy with little curly tails; a high-protein crop from the Andes.
items.alt: Trendy in health salads, it's gluten-free and technically a seed related to spinach.

items.name: soybean
items.description: A protein-rich bean made into tofu, soy sauce and soy milk
items.clue: A legume made into tofu, a dark salty sauce and a dairy-free milk.
items.alt: Steamed in fuzzy green pods and salted as edamame; huge amounts are grown to feed livestock and make cooking oil.

items.name: chickpea
items.description: A round beige bean, also called garbanzo, mashed into hummus
items.clue: A round, beige legume with a little beak-like point, mashed into hummus.
items.alt: Also called garbanzo; ground and shaped into falafel or roasted until crunchy.

items.name: lentil
items.description: A small flat lens-shaped legume, red, green or brown, cooked in soups
items.clue: Small, flat, lens-shaped legumes in red, green or brown, cooked into dal.
items.alt: Doesn't need soaking before cooking; a cheap protein in hearty soups and Indian stews.

items.name: kidney bean
items.description: A large dark red kidney-shaped bean, used in chili
items.clue: Dark red, glossy and curved like an organ in your lower back; essential in chili con carne.
items.alt: Must be boiled hard because raw ones are toxic; often served with rice in Caribbean dishes.

items.name: sunflower seed
items.description: A small seed in a black-and-white striped shell from sunflowers
items.clue: Small, striped black-and-white shells cracked open with your teeth; baseball players spit out the husks.
items.alt: Birds love them at feeders; the kernels come from the giant face of a tall yellow summer bloom.

items.name: rye
items.description: A dark cereal grain used for dense rye bread and whiskey
items.clue: A tall cereal crop whose dark kernels make a dense, sour loaf flavoured with caraway.
items.alt: Grows in cold, poor soil and is used to make a spicy whiskey and pumpernickel.

items.name: basil
items.description: A sweet herb with large soft green leaves, used in pesto
items.clue: Bright green, soft fragrant leaves blended with pine nuts and olive oil into pesto.
items.alt: Torn over a margherita pizza with tomato and mozzarella; there are sweet Italian and Thai varieties.

items.name: mint
items.description: A cool refreshing herb with fresh green leaves, used in tea and gum
items.clue: Fresh, cooling leaves that flavour chewing gum, toothpaste and mojitos.
items.alt: Spreads aggressively through gardens by runners; its leaves are brewed into a refreshing tea.

items.name: parsley
items.description: A mild green herb with curly or flat leaves, used as garnish
items.clue: Bright green flat or curly leaves, often used as a garnish on the side of a plate.
items.alt: Chopped into tabbouleh and chewed to freshen breath; it opens a famous folk-song line followed by sage, rosemary and thyme.

items.name: cinnamon
items.description: A sweet brown spice from rolled tree bark, used in baking
items.clue: Rolled-up curls of brown bark, ground into a sweet, warm powder for buns and apple pie.
items.alt: Sprinkled on toast with sugar and on lattes; it comes from the inner bark of a tropical evergreen.

items.name: black pepper
items.description: A sharp spice of ground dried black peppercorns, paired with salt
items.clue: Tiny dark dried berries ground in a mill and shaken out next to the salt on every table.
items.alt: Makes you sneeze; it's cracked fresh over pasta and was once so valuable it was traded like money.

items.name: ginger
items.description: A spicy knobbly pale root used fresh or ground for zingy flavour
items.clue: A knobbly, pale brown root with a hot, zingy flavour, used in stir-fries and pink sushi pickles.
items.alt: Made into a fizzy ale and snap biscuits, it's also a remedy for an upset stomach and a word for red hair.

items.name: oregano
items.description: A dried earthy herb with small leaves, sprinkled on pizza
items.clue: Small dried green leaves sprinkled on pizza and stirred into tomato sauces.
items.alt: A Mediterranean member of the mint family whose earthy, slightly bitter taste is key in Greek and Italian cooking.

items.name: rosemary
items.description: A fragrant herb with needle-like leaves on woody stems, used with roasts
items.clue: Woody stems with needle-like, piney-smelling leaves, roasted with lamb and potatoes.
items.alt: Tradition says it's for remembrance; its stiff sprigs can be used as skewers on the grill.

items.name: thyme
items.description: A herb with tiny leaves on thin woody stems, earthy flavour
items.clue: Tiny leaves on thin woody stems with an earthy, lemony taste, used in stews and roast chicken.
items.alt: Sounds exactly like the word for what a clock measures; it's a classic part of a bouquet garni.

items.name: cilantro
items.description: A herb with flat lacy leaves and a citrusy taste, used in salsa
items.clue: A fresh, leafy green that tastes bright and citrusy to most people but like soap to some.
items.alt: Also called coriander; it tops tacos and salsa, and its dried seeds are used whole in curry.

items.name: vanilla
items.description: A sweet fragrant flavouring from the long dark pods of an orchid
items.clue: Long, thin, dark pods from an orchid, giving the most popular flavour of ice cream.
items.alt: Its extract is in almost every cookie and cake recipe; the word is also slang for plain or ordinary.

items.name: nutmeg
items.description: A warm sweet spice grated from a hard brown seed, used in eggnog
items.clue: A hard brown seed grated into eggnog and pumpkin pie.
items.alt: Its lacy red covering is a separate seasoning called mace; it was once so valuable that islands were traded for it.

items.name: dill
items.description: A feathery herb with thread-like leaves, used in pickles and fish
items.clue: Feathery, thread-like green fronds that flavour sour gherkins and pair with salmon.
items.alt: Its seeds and fronds give a distinctive taste to creamy potato salad and tzatziki.

items.name: sage
items.description: A herb with soft fuzzy grey-green leaves, used in stuffing
items.clue: Soft, fuzzy, grey-green leaves used in turkey stuffing and crisped in brown butter.
items.alt: Shares its name with a wise old person; dried bundles of it are burned for their smoke.

items.name: saffron
items.description: An expensive red-orange spice from crocus flower threads, colours rice yellow
items.clue: Thin red-orange threads picked by hand from crocus blooms; the most expensive seasoning by weight.
items.alt: Gives paella and risotto their golden-yellow colour; it takes thousands of tiny stigmas to make a small amount.

items.name: clove
items.description: A small dried nail-shaped brown flower bud, strong warm spice
items.clue: Small, dark brown, nail-shaped dried buds pushed into a glazed ham or an orange.
items.alt: Its oil numbs a toothache; it goes into mulled wine and has a strong, warm smell.

items.name: turmeric
items.description: A bright yellow-orange spice from a ground root, used in curry
items.clue: A bright yellow-orange powder from a root that gives curry its golden colour.
items.alt: Stains everything yellow; it's in golden milk lattes and is praised for anti-inflammatory curcumin.

items.name: mustard
items.description: A tangy yellow condiment made from ground mustard seeds
items.clue: Tiny round seeds ground into a yellow paste squeezed onto hot dogs.
items.alt: Its bright yellow fields bloom in spring, and the sharp condiment comes in Dijon and wholegrain styles.

items.name: oak tree
items.description: A large sturdy hardwood tree with lobed leaves that grows acorns
items.clue: Big, strong and long-lived, with lobed leaves; squirrels collect the acorns it drops.
items.alt: Its hard timber was used for sailing ships and wine barrels, and it's a symbol of strength in many countries.

items.name: maple tree
items.description: A tree with five-pointed leaves, red in autumn, tapped for syrup
items.clue: Its five-pointed leaves turn brilliant red and orange in autumn, and its sap is boiled into a sweet syrup.
items.alt: Its winged seeds spin down like little helicopters, and its leaf appears on a national flag.

items.name: pine tree
items.description: An evergreen conifer with long needles and woody pine cones
items.clue: An evergreen with long, thin needles in bundles and woody cones.
items.alt: Smells fresh and resinous; its sticky sap makes turpentine and its soft lumber is used everywhere.

items.name: palm tree
items.description: A tropical tree with a tall bare trunk and huge leaves at top
items.clue: A tall, thin trunk with no branches and a tuft of huge fan or feather leaves at the top, found on tropical beaches.
items.alt: Coconuts and dates grow on it; it sways in hurricanes and appears on many island postcards.

items.name: birch tree
items.description: A slender tree with peeling white papery bark
items.clue: Slender, with peeling white papery bark marked with black lines.
items.alt: Its bark was used to build canoes, and its sap can be tapped in spring like syrup.

items.name: willow tree
items.description: A tree with long drooping branches that trail near water
items.clue: Has long, drooping branches that hang down to the water; a weeping variety is famous.
items.alt: Grows beside rivers; its bark was the original source of the chemical in aspirin, and its twigs are woven into baskets.

items.name: redwood
items.description: A gigantic reddish-barked conifer, the tallest trees, in California
items.clue: The tallest living things on earth: giant conifers in the foggy coastal forests of California.
items.alt: Its thick, spongy, rust-coloured bark resists fire, and some are over two thousand years old.

items.name: elm tree
items.description: A tall shady tree with saw-edged leaves, killed by Dutch elm disease
items.clue: A tall shade-giver with a vase-shaped crown that once lined many town streets.
items.alt: Millions were wiped out in the 20th century by a beetle-spread fungal disease named after the Netherlands.

items.name: eucalyptus tree
items.description: A fragrant Australian gum tree whose leaves koalas eat
items.clue: A tall Australian evergreen with peeling bark and long, strongly scented leaves.
items.alt: Koalas eat almost nothing but its leaves, and its oil is in cough drops and vapour rubs.

items.name: baobab tree
items.description: An African tree with a massive swollen bottle-shaped trunk and stubby branches
items.clue: Has a huge, swollen trunk that stores water and stubby branches that look like roots; found in Africa.
items.alt: Sometimes called the upside-down one; its dry, powdery pod pulp is high in vitamin C.

items.name: cedar tree
items.description: A large evergreen conifer with fragrant reddish wood used for chests
items.clue: A large conifer with fragrant reddish timber used in closets and chests to repel moths.
items.alt: Appears on Lebanon's flag; its rot-resistant timber is used for shingles, fences and saunas.

items.name: bonsai tree
items.description: A miniature tree grown and pruned in a small pot
items.clue: A miniature version grown in a shallow pot, carefully pruned and wired to look old.
items.alt: A Japanese art form in which a woody plant is kept tiny for decades on a windowsill.

items.name: christmas tree
items.description: An evergreen fir decorated with lights and ornaments for Christmas
items.clue: An evergreen brought indoors in December and covered with lights, ornaments and a star on top.
items.alt: Presents get stacked underneath it; real ones drop needles on the carpet and fake ones come out of a box.

items.name: apple tree
items.description: A fruit tree with pink-white blossoms that grows apples in orchards
items.clue: Grows in orchards, covered in pink-white blossoms in spring and crunchy red or green produce in autumn.
items.alt: A famous story says one dropped something on Isaac Newton's head and inspired his idea of gravity.

items.name: cypress tree
items.description: A tall narrow column-shaped evergreen conifer, common in Mediterranean landscapes
items.clue: A tall, narrow, dark green conifer shaped like a column, lining roads in Italy and graveyards.
items.alt: A swamp variety sends knobbly 'knees' up out of the water in the bayous of the southern US.

items.name: sycamore tree
items.description: A large tree with mottled peeling bark and broad maple-like leaves
items.clue: Has mottled bark that peels to show white, cream and green patches like camouflage.
items.alt: Its seeds hang in spiky balls, and in a Bible story a short man climbed one to see over a crowd.

items.name: aspen tree
items.description: A white-barked tree whose round leaves tremble and flutter in breeze
items.clue: Slender with white bark; its round leaves tremble and flutter in the slightest breeze.
items.alt: A whole grove can be one organism joined by underground roots, and its leaves turn bright gold in fall.

items.name: magnolia tree
items.description: A tree with large showy white or pink fragrant flowers
items.clue: Bears huge, waxy white or pink cup-shaped blooms in spring and has glossy, leathery leaves.
items.alt: A symbol of the American South; its very fragrant blossoms are among the most ancient bloom types on earth.

items.name: rose
items.description: A fragrant flower with layered petals, often red, on thorny stems
items.clue: Has thorny stems and layered, velvety petals, often red; a dozen are given on Valentine's Day.
items.alt: A symbol of love and romance; its fragrant oil goes into perfume and its hips make a vitamin-rich tea.

items.name: sunflower
items.description: A very tall flower with a big yellow head that faces the sun
items.clue: Very tall, with a huge yellow head that turns to face the light; its seeds are a popular snack.
items.alt: Grown in vast fields for cooking oil; its giant dark centre is packed with striped seeds and ringed by golden petals.

items.name: tulip
items.description: A cup-shaped spring flower on a straight stem, grown from bulbs
items.clue: A cup-shaped spring bloom on a straight stem, grown from a bulb in bright colours.
items.alt: Fields of it in Holland draw tourists, and its bulbs once caused a famous financial bubble.

items.name: daisy
items.description: A small flower with white petals around a yellow centre
items.clue: White petals around a yellow centre; kids pull the petals off saying 'loves me, loves me not'.
items.alt: A small, simple bloom that dots lawns; you can link them into chains to wear as a crown.

items.name: dandelion
items.description: A yellow weed flower that turns into a white fluffy seed puffball
items.clue: A yellow lawn weed that turns into a fluffy white ball of seeds you blow on to make a wish.
items.alt: Its jagged leaves are edible in salads, and its name comes from the French for a big cat's tooth.

items.name: lily
items.description: A large trumpet-shaped flower with six petals, often white
items.clue: A tall bloom with large trumpet-shaped petals and prominent stamens, often white; toxic to cats.
items.alt: Associated with funerals and Easter; frogs sit on the floating pads of a water variety.

items.name: orchid
items.description: An exotic tropical flower with unusual symmetrical petals, grown as houseplant
items.clue: Exotic, elegant blooms with unusual shapes, often grown as houseplants in pots of bark.
items.alt: A huge plant family: vanilla comes from one, and some mimic insects to attract pollinators.

items.name: daffodil
items.description: A yellow spring flower with a trumpet-shaped centre, grown from bulbs
items.clue: A bright yellow spring bloom with a trumpet-shaped centre, grown from a bulb.
items.alt: Often among the first to appear after winter; a poet wandered lonely as a cloud and saw a host of them.

items.name: lavender
items.description: A purple flower on spikes with a calming scent, used in soaps
items.clue: Spikes of tiny purple blooms with a calming scent, used in soaps and sachets.
items.alt: Fields of it turn the hills of southern France purple, and its oil is used to help you sleep.

items.name: poppy
items.description: A red flower with papery petals and a black centre, for remembrance
items.clue: Delicate bright red petals with a black centre; worn on lapels to remember fallen soldiers.
items.alt: Its seeds are sprinkled on bagels and muffins, and in a famous film a field of them puts travellers to sleep.

items.name: carnation
items.description: A frilly-edged flower, pink, white or red, worn in buttonholes
items.clue: Ruffled, frilly petals with jagged edges, often pink, red or white; a buttonhole favourite.
items.alt: A long-lasting cut bloom; white ones can be dyed any colour by standing them in coloured water.

items.name: marigold
items.description: A bushy orange or yellow flower with ruffled petals, garden border
items.clue: Bright orange or yellow pom-pom blooms with a strong smell, planted to keep pests off vegetables.
items.alt: Strung into garlands for Indian weddings and used to decorate altars for the Day of the Dead.

items.name: violet
items.description: A small purple flower with heart-shaped leaves, low to the ground
items.clue: A small, delicate purple bloom with heart-shaped leaves, growing low in shady spots.
items.alt: Its name is also a bluish-purple colour and a girl's name, and a classic rhyme pairs it with red roses.

items.name: hibiscus
items.description: A large showy tropical flower with a long central stamen, often red
items.clue: A large, showy tropical bloom with five petals and a long stamen sticking out, often red or pink.
items.alt: Worn behind the ear in Hawaii and brewed into a tart crimson tea.

items.name: lotus
items.description: A pink or white flower that blooms on water from muddy ponds
items.clue: A pink or white bloom that rises from muddy water on a long stalk, sacred in Buddhism.
items.alt: Its big round leaves repel water, and a famous cross-legged yoga position is named after it.

items.name: cherry blossom
items.description: Pale pink spring blossoms on cherry trees, celebrated in Japan
items.clue: Delicate pink petals that cover trees briefly in spring, then fall like snow.
items.alt: In Japan people picnic beneath them during hanami, and Washington DC holds a famous festival for them.

items.name: hydrangea
items.description: A shrub with big round clusters of blue, pink or white flowers
items.clue: Big round clusters of small blooms whose colour changes from pink to blue depending on the soil.
items.alt: A garden shrub with huge mophead pom-poms that dry well for wreaths.

items.name: buttercup
items.description: A small shiny bright yellow cup-shaped wildflower of meadows
items.clue: A small, glossy yellow wild bloom in grassy meadows; held under your chin, its glow is said to reveal a liking for dairy.
items.alt: Its five waxy petals are so shiny they reflect light, and it's mildly poisonous to cattle.

items.name: pansy
items.description: A small garden flower with velvety petals marked like a face
items.clue: Has round petals with a dark, face-like blotch in the middle, in purple, yellow and blue.
items.alt: A cheerful bedding plant that tolerates cold; its name comes from the French word for 'thought'.

items.name: iris
items.description: A tall flower with purple petals, three upright and three drooping
items.clue: A tall bloom with three upright petals and three drooping ones, often purple-blue, sharing its name with part of the eye.
items.alt: Its stylised shape is the fleur-de-lis, and it's named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow.

items.name: grass
items.description: Thin green blades covering lawns and fields, mowed short
items.clue: Green blades that cover lawns and fields; you mow it and it stains your knees.
items.alt: Cows and sheep graze on it all day; it smells fresh when just cut and gives some people hay fever.

items.name: moss
items.description: A soft low green carpet growing on damp rocks and trees
items.clue: Soft, green and spongy, growing in a carpet on rocks, logs and the shady side of trunks.
items.alt: Has no roots or seeds, spreads by spores, and a rolling stone famously gathers none.

items.name: cactus
items.description: A spiny desert plant with thick fleshy stems storing water
items.clue: A spiny, thick-stemmed desert dweller that stores water and has sharp needles.
items.alt: A popular low-maintenance windowsill pot because it needs almost no watering; some kinds have edible pads.

items.name: seaweed
items.description: Algae growing in the sea, used to wrap sushi
items.clue: Slimy green or brown algae that wash up on beaches and wrap around your legs when you swim in the ocean.
items.alt: Dried sheets of it wrap sushi rolls, and giant kelp forests of it grow underwater.

items.name: mushroom
items.description: A fungus with a cap and stem growing in damp soil
items.clue: A fungus with a stem and an umbrella-shaped cap that springs up after rain.
items.alt: Button and portobello kinds are sliced onto pizza, but some wild ones are deadly poisonous.

items.name: fern
items.description: A shade plant with feathery fronds that uncurl, reproduces by spores
items.clue: Has feathery, lacy fronds that unroll from curled fiddleheads, growing in shady forests.
items.alt: An ancient green that reproduces with spores on the undersides of its fronds instead of seeds.

items.name: ivy
items.description: A climbing evergreen vine that covers walls with leaves
items.clue: A climbing vine with glossy lobed leaves that covers old brick walls.
items.alt: Famous for draping the buildings of old universities; a poisonous relative gives you an itchy rash.

items.name: bamboo
items.description: A giant fast-growing woody grass with hollow jointed stems, eaten by pandas
items.clue: Tall, hollow, jointed green stalks that grow incredibly fast; pandas eat it.
items.alt: Used for scaffolding, flooring and chopsticks, it's actually a giant grass.

items.name: venus flytrap
items.description: A carnivorous plant with toothed leaf traps that snap shut on insects
items.clue: Carnivorous, with jaw-like leaves fringed with spikes that snap shut on insects.
items.alt: Native only to boggy areas of the Carolinas, it digests bugs because its soil lacks nutrients.

items.name: aloe vera
items.description: A succulent with thick spiky leaves holding soothing gel for burns
items.clue: Thick, spiky, fleshy leaves filled with a clear gel that soothes sunburn.
items.alt: A succulent kept on kitchen windowsills whose slimy gel goes into lotions and some juices.

items.name: clover
items.description: A small low plant with three round leaflets; four is lucky
items.clue: Small, with leaves made of three round leaflets; finding one with four is good luck.
items.alt: Grows in lawns with little white or pink pom-pom blooms that bees love; a symbol of Ireland.

items.name: hay
items.description: Dried cut grass stored in bales to feed horses and cows
items.clue: Dried grass cut and baled in summer to feed horses and cattle through the winter.
items.alt: Stacked in big round bales in fields and barns; finding a needle in a pile of it is proverbially hard.

items.name: pine cone
items.description: The woody scaly seed cone that falls from pine trees
items.clue: A brown, woody, scaly thing that falls from evergreens and holds seeds between its scales.
items.alt: Kids collect them in autumn for crafts and bird feeders, and its scales open up when the weather is dry.

items.name: leaf
items.description: A flat green part of a plant that falls in autumn
items.clue: Flat and green, it grows on a branch and turns red or yellow before falling in autumn.
items.alt: Kids press them in heavy volumes to dry; it makes energy from sunlight through photosynthesis.

items.name: tumbleweed
items.description: A dried bushy plant that breaks off and rolls across deserts
items.clue: A dried-out ball of branches that breaks off and rolls across the desert in the wind.
items.alt: Shows up in old cowboy films blowing through an empty town to show nobody's around.

items.name: mistletoe
items.description: A parasitic plant with white berries, hung for kissing at Christmas
items.clue: A parasitic evergreen with white berries, hung in doorways at holiday time so people kiss beneath it.
items.alt: Grows in balls on the branches of other trees, stealing their water; ancient druids considered it sacred.

items.name: holly
items.description: An evergreen shrub with spiky glossy leaves and red berries, Christmas decoration
items.clue: Spiky, glossy, dark green leaves with bright red berries, used for winter holiday decorations.
items.alt: A carol says to deck the halls with boughs of it; its berries are poisonous to people.

items.name: sugarcane
items.description: A tall thick jointed grass whose sweet juice is made into sugar
items.clue: A tall, thick, jointed grass grown in the tropics and crushed for its sweet juice.
items.alt: Its stalks are chewed raw in many countries and refined into white crystals; rum is distilled from its molasses.

items.name: bread
items.description: A baked loaf of wheat flour dough, sliced for sandwiches and toast
items.clue: Baked from flour, water and yeast into loaves you slice for sandwiches and toast.
items.alt: Comes in white, wholemeal and sourdough, and ducks get fed its crusts in the park.

items.name: pasta
items.description: Italian wheat dough noodles like spaghetti, boiled and served with sauce
items.clue: Durum wheat dough shaped into spaghetti, penne or macaroni, boiled and served with sauce.
items.alt: Italians cook it al dente, and it comes in hundreds of shapes like bowties and shells.

items.name: popcorn
items.description: Corn kernels that puff and pop when heated, a movie snack
items.clue: Dried maize kernels that burst into white fluffy puffs when heated; eaten at the movies.
items.alt: Made in a microwave bag or a kettle at fairs, usually with butter and salt; it's a whole-grain snack.

items.name: french fries
items.description: Thin strips of potato deep-fried until crisp, served hot with ketchup
items.clue: Long, thin strips of potato cooked in hot oil until crispy, served with ketchup.
items.alt: Served beside burgers at drive-throughs in a paper carton; Belgians dip them in mayonnaise.

items.name: potato chips
items.description: Thin crispy fried potato slices sold salted in bags
items.clue: Thin, crispy, salted slices of spud cooked in oil and sold in crinkly bags.
items.alt: Come in flavours like salt and vinegar or sour cream and onion, and are called crisps in Britain.

items.name: peanut butter
items.description: A thick brown spread of ground roasted peanuts, for sandwiches
items.clue: A thick, sticky spread made by grinding roasted legumes, paired with jelly in sandwiches.
items.alt: Comes smooth or crunchy, sticks to the roof of your mouth, and is used to hide pills for dogs.

items.name: chocolate
items.description: A sweet brown treat made from roasted cacao beans and sugar
items.clue: Sweet, brown and melty, made from roasted cacao seeds; given in heart-shaped boxes.
items.alt: Comes in dark, milk and white varieties, and it's hidden behind the doors of advent calendars.

items.name: sugar
items.description: Sweet white crystals refined from sugarcane or sugar beets
items.clue: Sweet white crystals refined from cane or beets, stirred into tea and coffee.
items.alt: Spooned into baking; too much rots your teeth, and candy floss is spun from it.

items.name: flour
items.description: A fine white powder of ground wheat, used for baking
items.clue: A fine white powder ground from wheat; the main ingredient in bread, cake and pancakes.
items.alt: Sold in paper sacks for baking; it's sifted and dusted onto the counter before rolling out dough.

items.name: cereal
items.description: Breakfast flakes or puffs of grain eaten from a bowl with milk
items.clue: Crunchy flakes or loops poured into a bowl with milk for breakfast.
items.alt: Sold in colourful boxes with cartoon mascots and sometimes a toy prize inside.

items.name: oatmeal
items.description: A warm soft porridge of cooked oats eaten for breakfast
items.clue: A warm, soft porridge of rolled flakes cooked with milk or water and topped with brown sugar.
items.alt: A hearty breakfast bowl that three bears in a fairy tale left to cool; often topped with raisins.

items.name: tortilla
items.description: A thin flat round bread of corn or wheat for tacos
items.clue: A thin, round flatbread of corn or wheat used to wrap tacos and burritos.
items.alt: Warmed on a griddle and folded around fillings in Mexican cooking; cut into wedges and baked into crunchy chips.

items.name: ketchup
items.description: A thick red sweet tomato sauce for dipping fries
items.clue: A thick red tomato sauce squeezed onto burgers and fries.
items.alt: Comes in a glass bottle you have to whack on the bottom; a classic condiment made with sugar and vinegar.

items.name: jam
items.description: A sweet thick fruit spread cooked with sugar, eaten on toast
items.clue: A sweet spread of crushed berries cooked with sugar, spread on toast.
items.alt: Made by boiling down summer produce with pectin and sealing it in jars; it's also a word for being stuck in traffic.

items.name: pickle
items.description: A cucumber preserved in sour vinegar brine, crunchy and salty
items.clue: A cucumber preserved in sour vinegar brine, crunchy and served beside a sandwich.
items.alt: Comes in dill or sweet varieties in a jar, and the word also means being in a tricky situation.

items.name: tofu
items.description: A soft white block of pressed soybean curd
items.clue: Soft white blocks made from curdled soy milk; a meat substitute in stir-fries.
items.alt: Bland on its own but soaks up flavour; it comes in silken and firm styles and is popular with vegans.

items.name: maple syrup
items.description: A sweet amber syrup boiled from maple tree sap, poured on pancakes
items.clue: A sweet amber liquid poured over pancakes and waffles, boiled down from tree sap.
items.alt: Tapped from trunks in late winter; it takes about forty litres of sap to make one litre, and it's graded by colour.

items.name: olive oil
items.description: A golden-green oil pressed from olives, used for cooking
items.clue: A golden-green liquid fat pressed from small Mediterranean drupes and drizzled over salads and pasta.
items.alt: The base of Mediterranean cooking; the best is labelled extra virgin and cold-pressed.

items.name: raisin
items.description: A small wrinkly dried grape, sweet and chewy
items.clue: Small, wrinkly, dark dried grapes eaten as a snack or baked into cookies.
items.alt: Comes in little red boxes in lunchboxes and is swirled into cinnamon loaves; it's what a vine's harvest becomes after drying in the sun.

items.name: applesauce
items.description: A smooth sweet purée of cooked mashed apples
items.clue: A smooth puree of cooked orchard produce, eaten by toddlers or served with pork chops.
items.alt: Comes in squeeze pouches and little cups, and can replace oil in baking.

items.name: pretzel
items.description: A twisted knot-shaped baked bread snack sprinkled with coarse salt
items.clue: A twisted knot of dough baked with a shiny brown crust and sprinkled with coarse salt.
items.alt: Sold soft at stadium stands with mustard, or as small crunchy snacks in a bag.

items.name: salad
items.description: A cold dish of mixed raw leafy greens and vegetables with dressing
items.clue: A bowl of raw leafy greens, tomato and cucumber tossed with dressing.
items.alt: Caesar, garden and Greek are kinds; it's usually eaten as a healthy starter with a fork.

items.name: hummus
items.description: A creamy dip of mashed chickpeas, tahini, lemon and garlic
items.clue: A creamy dip of mashed chickpeas, tahini, lemon and garlic, scooped up with pita.
items.alt: A Middle Eastern spread often drizzled with olive oil and paprika and served with carrot sticks.

items.name: guacamole
items.description: A green dip of mashed avocado with lime, onion and chili
items.clue: A green dip of mashed avocado, lime, onion and cilantro, served with tortilla chips.
items.alt: Made fresh in a stone mortar at Mexican restaurants; it turns brown if it's left out.

items.name: tea
items.description: A hot drink brewed by steeping dried tea leaves in water
items.clue: A hot brew made by steeping dried leaves in boiling water, served with milk or lemon.
items.alt: Comes in green, black and herbal varieties, and the British have it in the afternoon with biscuits.

items.name: coffee
items.description: A hot dark bitter caffeinated drink brewed from roasted ground beans
items.clue: A hot, dark, bitter brew made from roasted ground beans that wakes you up in the morning.
items.alt: Served as espresso, latte or cappuccino in cafes; its caffeine keeps people going.

items.name: orange juice
items.description: A sweet orange drink squeezed from oranges, served at breakfast
items.clue: Squeezed from citrus, it's sweet and tangy and served cold at breakfast, with or without pulp.
items.alt: Full of vitamin C, it tastes terrible right after you brush your teeth.

items.name: apple juice
items.description: A clear golden sweet drink pressed from apples
items.clue: Golden, clear and sweet, pressed from crunchy orchard produce and sold in kids' boxes with straws.
items.alt: Cloudy or clear, it's given to toddlers in sippy cups and can be fermented into cider.

items.name: lemonade
items.description: A sweet-sour drink of lemon juice, sugar and water
items.clue: A cold sweet-and-sour mix of squeezed yellow citrus, sugar and water, sold at kids' stands in summer.
items.alt: A saying tells you what to make when life hands you something sour; it can be pink or fizzy.

items.name: hot chocolate
items.description: A warm sweet drink of cocoa and milk, topped with marshmallows
items.clue: A warm, sweet, creamy mug of cocoa and milk topped with marshmallows or whipped cream.
items.alt: Sipped to warm up after sledding or ice skating on cold winter days.

items.name: wine
items.description: An alcoholic drink of fermented grapes, red or white
items.clue: An alcoholic beverage made from fermented grapes, red or white, served in stemmed glasses.
items.alt: Made in vineyards and aged in oak barrels; people swirl and sniff it before sipping.

items.name: beer
items.description: A foamy alcoholic drink brewed from malted barley and hops
items.clue: A fizzy alcoholic beverage brewed from malted barley and hops, served with a foamy head.
items.alt: Served in pints at pubs and in cans at barbecues; Germany celebrates it at Oktoberfest.

items.name: coconut water
items.description: The clear thin liquid drained from inside young green coconuts
items.clue: A clear, slightly sweet liquid from inside young green tropical palm drupes, sipped through a straw.
items.alt: Marketed as a natural sports beverage full of electrolytes; it's tapped from inside a hard shell.

items.name: almond milk
items.description: A white dairy-free milk made by blending almonds with water
items.clue: A dairy-free white liquid made by blending soaked nuts with water and straining it.
items.alt: Poured over cereal or into lattes by vegans and the lactose intolerant; sold in sweetened and unsweetened cartons.

items.name: smoothie
items.description: A thick cold blended drink of fruit, yogurt or ice
items.clue: A thick, cold blend of banana and berries, sometimes with yogurt, sipped through a straw.
items.alt: Whizzed up in a blender for breakfast or after the gym; green ones include spinach or kale.

items.name: grape juice
items.description: A sweet purple non-alcoholic drink pressed from grapes
items.clue: Sweet, dark purple and non-alcoholic, pressed from vineyard clusters; kids sip it from boxes.
items.alt: Stains clothes purple, and some churches serve it instead of wine at communion.

items.name: paper
items.description: Thin flat sheets made from wood pulp for writing and printing
items.clue: Thin, flat white sheets made from wood pulp that you write and print on.
items.alt: Comes in reams for the printer; you can fold it into planes and cranes, or get a cut from its edge.

items.name: cotton
items.description: Soft white fluffy plant fibre spun into cloth for t-shirts
items.clue: Soft, white, fluffy fibres from a boll, spun into thread for t-shirts and towels.
items.alt: Picked from bushy fields in the American South; little balls of it are used to remove makeup.

items.name: wood
items.description: Hard material cut from tree trunks, used for building and furniture
items.clue: The hard, fibrous stuff of trunks, cut into planks for building houses and furniture.
items.alt: It burns in fireplaces, has a grain and knots, and termites love to eat it.

items.name: cardboard
items.description: Thick stiff layered paperboard used to make boxes
items.clue: Thick, stiff, brown layered sheets folded into shipping boxes.
items.alt: Corrugated with a wavy middle layer; kids turn big boxes of it into forts.

items.name: rope
items.description: Thick strong cord of twisted plant fibres used for tying
items.clue: Thick strands of fibre twisted together, used for tying up boats, climbing and tug of war.
items.alt: Traditionally made from hemp, sisal or jute; sailors tie it into many kinds of knots.

items.name: cork
items.description: Light spongy bark of cork oak, used as bottle stoppers
items.clue: The light, spongy bark of an oak, used to seal wine bottles.
items.alt: It floats and is pressed into boards you pin notes to; it's stripped from the trunk without harming the living tree.

items.name: rubber
items.description: A stretchy bouncy material from rubber tree sap, used in tyres
items.clue: Stretchy, bouncy stuff made from the milky latex sap tapped from tropical trees; used in tyres.
items.alt: Bands of it hold things together, and erasers, balloons and wellington boots are made of it.

items.name: linen
items.description: A cool crisp fabric woven from flax plant fibres
items.clue: A crisp, cool fabric woven from flax fibres, used for summer clothes and tablecloths.
items.alt: It wrinkles easily, and sheets and napkins are often called by its name even when made of cotton.

items.name: book
items.description: Bound printed paper pages with a cover, for reading
items.clue: Many printed pages bound between covers, with a story or information to read.
items.alt: You borrow them from a library and line them up on shelves; novels and dictionaries are kinds.

items.name: pencil
items.description: A wooden writing stick with a graphite core and eraser
items.clue: A thin wooden stick with a graphite core used for writing, often with an eraser on the end.
items.alt: Kids sharpen it before tests, and number two ones are used to fill in answer bubbles.

items.name: newspaper
items.description: Large folded printed sheets of daily news on cheap paper
items.clue: Large folded printed sheets with daily headlines, delivered to doorsteps in the morning.
items.alt: Has sections for sports, comics and crosswords, and the ink rubs off on your fingers.

items.name: toilet paper
items.description: Soft thin paper on a roll for wiping in the bathroom
items.clue: Soft, thin tissue on a roll hanging in the bathroom.
items.alt: People panic-bought it early in the pandemic, and pranksters drape it over trees.

items.name: wicker basket
items.description: A basket woven from willow or cane twigs, for carrying
items.clue: A woven container made of willow twigs or rattan, used for picnics and laundry.
items.alt: A girl in a red hood carried one through the woods to her grandmother; eggs are collected in it at Easter.

items.name: jeans
items.description: Blue denim cotton trousers with rivets and pockets
items.clue: Blue denim trousers woven from cotton, with rivets and pockets.
items.alt: First made for miners in the gold rush; they fade and get comfier the more you wear them.

items.name: toothpick
items.description: A tiny thin pointed wooden stick for cleaning between teeth
items.clue: A tiny, thin, pointed sliver of birch used to dig food out from between your molars after a meal.
items.alt: Holds club sandwiches together and spears olives in cocktails.

items.name: chopsticks
items.description: A pair of thin wooden or bamboo sticks for eating
items.clue: A pair of thin wooden or bamboo rods used to pick up bites of noodles and sushi.
items.alt: Held in one hand, these two utensils are standard in East Asian cooking; you shouldn't stand them upright in rice.

categories.label: mineral
categories.description: A man-made object, a machine, a rock, a metal or a place

groups.label: vehicle
groups.description: Something that carries people or goods from one spot to another on roads, rails, water, through the air or into orbit, like a car, train, boat or plane.

groups.label: electronic device or appliance
groups.description: A machine that runs on electricity or batteries, from gadgets with screens and buttons to kitchen and laundry appliances.

groups.label: furniture or household object
groups.description: Something found around the home, such as furniture, bedding, bathroom fixtures, dishes, cutlery and cookware.

groups.label: tool or school supply
groups.description: A handheld implement for building, fixing, gardening or sewing, or something used in class for writing, drawing, measuring and reading.

groups.label: clothing or accessory
groups.description: Something you wear or carry on your body, such as garments, footwear, jewelry, eyewear and bags.

groups.label: toy, game or sports gear
groups.description: Something children or players use for fun, play, tabletop games or sport, such as dolls, balls, cards and outdoor play equipment.

groups.label: musical instrument
groups.description: Something you play to make music by striking, plucking, bowing, blowing into or squeezing it.

groups.label: building or place
groups.description: A structure or location that people live in, visit, work in or gather at, such as a home, landmark, venue or public building.

groups.label: nature, space or weather
groups.description: A natural feature of the landscape or sea, an object in the sky or outer space, or a weather event.

groups.label: material, metal or gem
groups.description: A raw substance or material, such as a metal, a precious stone, rock, a liquid, or a building material.

items.name: car
items.description: A small four-wheeled motor vehicle for carrying a few people on roads
items.clue: It has four wheels, a steering wheel and seats for about five people, and most families park one in the driveway or garage to drive to work and the shops.
items.alt: You fill it up with gasoline or charge it overnight, buckle a seatbelt inside it, and get stuck with it in rush-hour traffic.

items.name: bus
items.description: A long road vehicle that carries many passengers along a set route
items.clue: A long passenger carrier with many rows of seats that drives along a set route, stopping at shelters to let people on and off.
items.alt: Kids often ride a big yellow one to class each morning, and in cities you tap a card or pay a fare when you climb aboard.

items.name: truck
items.description: A large motor vehicle with a cargo bed or trailer for hauling goods
items.clue: A big, heavy road machine with a driver's cab in front and a large open bed or box behind, used for hauling cargo and deliveries.
items.alt: Long-haul drivers spend days in these on highways moving goods between warehouses, and the pickup kind is popular with builders for carrying loads.

items.name: train
items.description: A long line of connected cars pulled by a locomotive along railway tracks
items.clue: A long line of connected cars that runs on steel rails, pulled by a locomotive and stopping at stations.
items.alt: Commuters ride it between platforms, and old steam versions puffed smoke and blew a whistle as they chugged along the tracks.

items.name: airplane
items.description: A winged aircraft with engines that flies passengers or cargo through the sky
items.clue: It has wings and jet engines, takes off from a runway, and carries passengers high above the clouds to faraway cities.
items.alt: You board it at a gate after security, fasten your seatbelt, and a pilot flies it while attendants hand out drinks.

items.name: helicopter
items.description: An aircraft lifted by spinning overhead rotor blades that can hover in place
items.clue: It has big spinning rotor blades on top and can take off straight up, hover in one spot and land on a rooftop pad.
items.alt: Used for rescues at sea, traffic reports and medical airlifts, it makes a loud chopping thump overhead and has a small tail rotor.

items.name: ship
items.description: A large engine-powered vessel that carries passengers or cargo across the sea
items.clue: A huge ocean-going craft that carries cargo containers or thousands of passengers across the sea, docking at ports.
items.alt: It has a hull, a deck, a captain at the helm and a heavy anchor, and the Titanic was a famous one that sank in 1912.

items.name: sailboat
items.description: A small boat pushed across water by wind in its cloth sails
items.clue: A small craft on the water that is pushed along by the wind catching a big triangle of cloth attached to a tall mast.
items.alt: You tack back and forth across a lake or bay in it, pulling ropes to trim the canvas, with no engine needed on a breezy day.

items.name: bicycle
items.description: A two-wheeled vehicle with pedals, powered by the rider's legs
items.clue: It has two wheels, pedals, a chain and handlebars, and you ride it by pushing with your feet to make it go.
items.alt: Kids learn to ride one with training wheels, and adults commute on it in dedicated lanes while wearing a helmet.

items.name: motorcycle
items.description: A two-wheeled motor vehicle with an engine, ridden by straddling the seat
items.clue: A two-wheeled machine with an engine that you straddle like a horse, steering with handlebars and twisting a grip to speed up.
items.alt: Riders wear leather jackets and full-face helmets on it, and it roars loudly down the highway, sometimes with a sidecar attached.

items.name: tractor
items.description: A slow, powerful farm vehicle with big rear wheels for pulling plows
items.clue: A farm machine with huge rear wheels and small front ones, used to pull plows, trailers and other equipment across fields.
items.alt: Often painted green or red, it chugs slowly along country roads while a farmer sits high up in its open seat or cab.

items.name: rocket
items.description: A tall engine-powered craft that blasts upward into outer space
items.clue: A tall, pointed craft that blasts off from a launch pad with fire and smoke to carry astronauts or satellites into orbit.
items.alt: It counts down from ten before liftoff, sheds stages as it climbs, and burns huge amounts of fuel to escape Earth's gravity.

items.name: submarine
items.description: A sealed vessel that travels underwater, diving beneath the ocean surface
items.clue: A long, cigar-shaped craft that dives deep underwater and travels beneath the ocean surface, using a periscope to look above.
items.alt: Navies use it to patrol silently below the waves, and its crew can stay hidden under the sea for months, steering by sonar.

items.name: ambulance
items.description: An emergency vehicle with sirens that rushes sick or injured people to hospital
items.clue: A white emergency van with flashing lights and a siren that rushes sick or injured people to the hospital.
items.alt: Paramedics ride in the back of it with a stretcher, oxygen and first-aid supplies, and other drivers pull over to let it pass.

items.name: fire truck
items.description: A big red emergency vehicle with ladders and hoses for fighting fires
items.clue: A big red emergency machine with ladders and hoses that races to put out blazes with its siren wailing.
items.alt: It carries a crew in helmets and heavy coats, pumps water from hydrants, and has an extending ladder to reach upper windows.

items.name: scooter
items.description: A small vehicle with a narrow footboard and handlebar, kick-pushed or motorized
items.clue: A narrow deck on two small wheels with a tall T-shaped handlebar, which you ride by pushing off the ground with one foot.
items.alt: Electric rental ones are left on city sidewalks and unlocked with a phone app, and the motorized kind is popular in Italy for zipping around.

items.name: phone
items.description: A small handheld device for calling, texting and using apps
items.clue: A small rectangular gadget with a touchscreen that you carry in your pocket to call people, send texts and take pictures.
items.alt: You charge it every night, scroll social media on it, and it rings or buzzes when someone wants to talk to you.

items.name: computer
items.description: A desktop machine with a separate monitor, keyboard and mouse for computing
items.clue: A machine with a monitor, keyboard and mouse that sits on a desk, used for typing documents, browsing the internet and running programs.
items.alt: It has a processor, memory and a hard drive inside a tower case, and offices are full of them for work and email.

items.name: laptop
items.description: A portable folding computer with a built-in screen and keyboard
items.clue: A portable machine that folds open like a clamshell, with a screen on the top half and a keyboard on the bottom.
items.alt: Students carry one in a bag to take notes in lectures, and it runs on a rechargeable battery with a trackpad instead of a mouse.

items.name: television
items.description: A large screen appliance for watching shows, movies and broadcast channels
items.clue: A big flat screen in the living room that families sit in front of to watch shows, movies, news and sports.
items.alt: You change its channels with a remote, and it used to be a bulky box with an antenna on top.

items.name: radio
items.description: A device that receives broadcast signals and plays music, news and talk aloud
items.clue: A box that picks up broadcasts through the air so you can listen to music, news and talk shows, often in the car.
items.alt: You tune it with a dial to stations on the FM or AM band, and DJs play songs on it between commercials.

items.name: camera
items.description: A device with a lens that takes photographs or records video
items.clue: You hold it up to your eye or look at its screen and press a button to take photographs.
items.alt: It has a lens, a shutter and a flash, and old ones used rolls of film that had to be developed.

items.name: tablet
items.description: A flat touchscreen computer without a keyboard, larger than a phone
items.clue: A thin, flat touchscreen slate bigger than a phone but without a keyboard, used for reading, watching videos and using apps.
items.alt: Kids often watch cartoons on one propped up in the car, and artists draw on it with a stylus.

items.name: headphones
items.description: A pair of small speakers worn over the ears for private listening
items.clue: A pair of padded cups joined by a band over your skull that you wear to listen to music privately.
items.alt: You plug them into a jack or connect them by Bluetooth, and some have noise cancelling for long flights.

items.name: remote control
items.description: A small handheld button pad for operating a television from across the room
items.clue: A small handheld stick with lots of buttons that you point at the TV to change channels and volume.
items.alt: It's always getting lost between the sofa cushions, and it runs on two AA batteries and works by infrared signal.

items.name: game console
items.description: A machine that connects to a television for playing video games with controllers
items.clue: A box you plug into the TV with handheld controllers so you can play racing, shooting and adventure titles on the big screen.
items.alt: Kids beg for the newest one at holiday time, and friends sit on the couch holding joysticks to compete against each other on screen.

items.name: microphone
items.description: A device that picks up voice or sound and converts it to signals
items.clue: You hold it up to your mouth or stand it in front of you so your voice gets louder through speakers.
items.alt: Singers grip one on stage, podcasters talk into one at a desk, and comedians sometimes drop it at the end of a show.

items.name: battery
items.description: A small cell that stores chemical energy and supplies electric power
items.clue: A small cylinder or block that stores electrical power, with a plus and minus end, and you put it into gadgets to make them run.
items.alt: Common sizes are AA and AAA, they eventually run flat and should be recycled, and a car has a big lead-acid one under the hood.

items.name: calculator
items.description: A small handheld device with number keys for doing arithmetic
items.clue: A small handheld gadget with number keys and a little display used to add, subtract, multiply and divide.
items.alt: Math students use it in exams to work out sums and square roots, and accountants keep one on their desk.

items.name: flashlight
items.description: A handheld battery-powered light that shines a beam in the dark
items.clue: A handheld tube with a bulb at one end that you switch on to see in the dark or during a power cut.
items.alt: You keep one in a drawer for emergencies and use its beam to find your way on a camping trip at night.

items.name: robot
items.description: A programmable machine that moves and performs tasks automatically, sometimes humanlike
items.clue: A machine that can move and do tasks by itself, sometimes built to look like a person with metal arms and a face.
items.alt: Factories use them to weld cars on assembly lines, and in movies they are mechanical helpers that talk in beeping voices.

items.name: light bulb
items.description: A glass bulb that glows to give light when screwed into a socket
items.clue: A glass globe that screws into a lamp or ceiling socket and glows when you flip the switch.
items.alt: Thomas Edison is famous for improving it, and in cartoons one appears above a character's head when they get an idea.

items.name: refrigerator
items.description: A tall cold kitchen appliance that keeps food and drinks chilled and fresh
items.clue: A tall cold box in the kitchen where you keep milk, vegetables and leftovers so they don't spoil.
items.alt: It has a freezer compartment, its door is often covered in magnets and kids' drawings, and it hums quietly day and night.

items.name: oven
items.description: A kitchen appliance with an enclosed hot box for baking and roasting
items.clue: A hot box in the kitchen with a door and racks inside, used for baking bread and cakes and roasting meat.
items.alt: You preheat it to 350 degrees, slide in a tray of cookies, and use mitts to take out the hot dish.

items.name: microwave
items.description: A small box appliance that heats food quickly using microwaves
items.clue: A small box on the kitchen counter that heats leftovers and pops popcorn in a few minutes on a spinning plate inside.
items.alt: It beeps when it's done, you must never put foil or forks in it, and a little window lets you watch your food turn.

items.name: toaster
items.description: A countertop appliance with slots that browns slices of bread
items.clue: A small kitchen gadget with slots on top where you drop slices of bread to brown them, and they pop up when done.
items.alt: You push down a lever, the coils inside glow orange, and breakfast pops out crispy and ready for butter.

items.name: blender
items.description: A kitchen appliance with spinning blades in a jar for mixing smoothies
items.clue: A tall jug on a motorized base with sharp spinning blades at the bottom, used to make smoothies and soups.
items.alt: It whirs loudly when you crush ice for milkshakes or puree fruit, and it has a lid you must hold down.

items.name: washing machine
items.description: A large appliance that cleans dirty clothes with water and soap
items.clue: A big white box in the laundry room that cleans your clothes with water and soap, spinning them around in a drum.
items.alt: You load dirty laundry through its round front door or top lid, add detergent, and it rinses and spins for about an hour.

items.name: vacuum cleaner
items.description: A machine that sucks up dust and dirt from floors and carpets
items.clue: A noisy machine you push around the house that sucks up dust and crumbs from carpets through a hose.
items.alt: It has a bag or dust cup that needs emptying, and some round ones roll around the floor on their own.

items.name: fan
items.description: An electric device with spinning blades that blows air to cool people
items.clue: It has spinning blades that blow cool air around a room on a hot day, and it can sit on a desk or hang from the ceiling.
items.alt: You switch it to low, medium or high speed, and some models turn their head from side to side to spread a breeze.

items.name: chair
items.description: A seat with legs and a back for one person to sit
items.clue: It has four legs, a seat and a back, and you sit on it at the dinner table or at a desk.
items.alt: Teachers tell students to push them in, and a musical party pastime with them always leaves someone standing.

items.name: table
items.description: A flat raised surface on legs for eating meals or placing things
items.clue: A flat top held up by legs where families eat dinner, play cards and put their plates.
items.alt: You set it with a cloth, cutlery and napkins, and everyone sits around it in the dining room.

items.name: bed
items.description: A large padded piece of furniture with a mattress for sleeping on
items.clue: A large padded frame with a mattress, sheets and pillows where you sleep at night.
items.alt: It can be twin, queen or king size, kids jump on it, and they imagine monsters hiding underneath it.

items.name: sofa
items.description: A long cushioned seat with a back and arms for several people
items.clue: A long, soft, cushioned seat in the living room where two or three people can sit together to watch TV.
items.alt: Guests sometimes sleep on it, and lost coins and remotes end up hidden between its cushions.

items.name: desk
items.description: A table with drawers used for writing, studying or working at
items.clue: A table with drawers where you sit to do homework, write or work on a computer.
items.alt: Office workers have one in a cubicle, and pupils each sit at a small one in a classroom.

items.name: lamp
items.description: A light fixture with a shade that stands on a table or floor
items.clue: It stands on a table or the floor with a shade on top and a bulb inside, and you switch it on to read at night.
items.alt: Aladdin rubbed an old oil one and a genie came out, and modern ones sit on bedside tables.

items.name: mirror
items.description: A sheet of reflective glass that shows your own reflection
items.clue: A sheet of shiny glass on the wall where you see your own reflection when you comb your hair.
items.alt: In the fairy tale the evil queen asks it who is the fairest of them all, and breaking one supposedly brings seven years of bad luck.

items.name: clock
items.description: A wall or shelf device with hands or digits that shows the time
items.clue: It hangs on the wall with a round face, numbers and two hands that point to the hour and minutes.
items.alt: It goes tick-tock, some have a cuckoo that pops out on the hour, and you set an alarm on one to wake up.

items.name: door
items.description: A hinged panel that opens and closes an entrance to a room or building
items.clue: A large hinged panel with a handle that you open to go into a room or a house and close behind you.
items.alt: Visitors knock on it or ring the bell beside it, and you lock it with a key at night.

items.name: window
items.description: A glass pane in a wall that lets in light and air
items.clue: A pane of clear glass set in a wall that lets daylight in and lets you look outside.
items.alt: You open it for fresh air, draw the curtains or blinds over it at night, and wipe the streaks off it and its sill.

items.name: pillow
items.description: A soft cushion for resting your head on while sleeping in bed
items.clue: A soft, stuffed cushion that you rest your head on in bed while you sleep.
items.alt: It goes inside a cotton case, kids have fights with them at sleepovers, and some are filled with feathers.

items.name: blanket
items.description: A large soft cloth covering that keeps you warm in bed
items.clue: A large, warm piece of soft fabric that you spread over yourself in bed or on the couch when you're cold.
items.alt: Toddlers drag around a favorite security one, and you might spread one on the grass for a picnic.

items.name: towel
items.description: An absorbent cloth for drying your body or hands after washing
items.clue: A thick, absorbent cloth you use to dry your body after a shower or bath.
items.alt: It hangs on a rail in the bathroom, you lie on a big striped one at the beach, and you dry dishes with a smaller one.

items.name: candle
items.description: A wax stick with a wick that burns with a small flame
items.clue: A stick of wax with a wick in the middle that you light to make a small flame for light or a nice smell.
items.alt: You blow them out on a birthday cake and make a wish, and people set them on the table for a romantic dinner.

items.name: key
items.description: A small notched metal piece that turns in a lock to open it
items.clue: A small notched piece of metal that you put into a lock and turn to open a door or start a car.
items.alt: You keep several on a ring in your pocket, and losing them means you might be locked out of your house.

items.name: bathtub
items.description: A large tub filled with water for bathing the whole body
items.clue: A large, long basin you fill with warm water and lie down in to soak and get clean, often with bubbles.
items.alt: It has a plug and a faucet at one end, toddlers splash with toys in it, and sometimes a curtained shower hangs above it.

items.name: toilet
items.description: A bathroom fixture with a bowl and seat that flushes away waste
items.clue: A porcelain seat over a bowl of water in the bathroom that you flush after using.
items.alt: It has a lid and a tank, you might need a plunger when it clogs, and a roll of paper hangs beside it.

items.name: broom
items.description: A long-handled brush with bristles for sweeping floors
items.clue: A long wooden handle with a bundle of stiff bristles at the end, used for sweeping dirt off the floor.
items.alt: Witches fly on one in stories, and you use it with a dustpan to tidy up the kitchen or porch.

items.name: bookshelf
items.description: A piece of furniture with horizontal shelves for holding books
items.clue: A tall wooden case with flat horizontal boards where you line up novels and display photos.
items.alt: Libraries and studies are lined with them, and you organize paperbacks on it by author or by color.

items.name: trash can
items.description: A container with a lid for throwing away garbage and waste
items.clue: A lidded container where you throw away garbage and food scraps, and you take it out to the curb each week.
items.alt: It stands under the sink or in a corner of the kitchen with a plastic liner bag, and it starts to smell if nobody empties it.

items.name: toothbrush
items.description: A small brush with a handle for cleaning your teeth
items.clue: A small plastic stick with bristles on one end that you use with minty paste to clean your mouth twice a day.
items.alt: Dentists recommend replacing it every three months, and electric ones vibrate or spin while you scrub your gums.

items.name: cup
items.description: A small drinking container with a handle for hot drinks like coffee
items.clue: A small container with a handle that you drink hot tea or coffee from.
items.alt: It sits on a saucer, holds about eight ounces, and is also a unit in baking recipes for measuring flour.

items.name: plate
items.description: A flat round dish that food is served and eaten from
items.clue: A flat, round dish that you put your food on to eat dinner.
items.alt: You stack them in the cupboard after washing, they're usually ceramic or china, and fancy dinners have a separate smaller one for salad.

items.name: bowl
items.description: A deep round dish for holding soup, cereal or other foods
items.clue: A round, deep dish you eat cereal, soup or ice cream from with a spoon.
items.alt: Goldfish sometimes live in a glass one, and you mix cake batter in a big one before baking.

items.name: spoon
items.description: An eating utensil with a small shallow scoop for soup and liquids
items.clue: A piece of cutlery with a small oval scoop at the end, used to eat soup and cereal or stir your tea.
items.alt: Babies are fed mashed food with a small one, and it comes in tea and table sizes for measuring medicine or sugar.

items.name: fork
items.description: An eating utensil with pointed prongs for picking up food
items.clue: A piece of cutlery with three or four pointed prongs used to stab food and lift it to your mouth.
items.alt: You twirl spaghetti on it, it is set to the left of your plate, and a road that splits in two is named after its shape.

items.name: knife
items.description: A utensil with a sharp blade for cutting food
items.clue: A piece of cutlery with a sharp blade and a handle used to cut food like meat and bread.
items.alt: Chefs keep a set of them in a wooden block, and you use a butter one to spread jam on bread.

items.name: pot
items.description: A deep metal cooking vessel with handles for boiling soup or pasta
items.clue: A deep round cooking vessel with handles and a lid, used on the stove to boil pasta or make soup.
items.alt: You fill it with water to boil eggs, and a big one is used for stews, chili and boiling lobsters.

items.name: frying pan
items.description: A shallow flat metal pan with a long handle for frying food
items.clue: A flat, shallow cooking dish with a long handle that you heat on the stove to cook eggs and bacon.
items.alt: It's often cast iron or non-stick, you flip omelets in it, and cartoon characters get bonked on the head with it.

items.name: kettle
items.description: A pot with a spout and handle for boiling water for tea
items.clue: You fill it with water and heat it until it whistles or clicks off, then pour the boiling water for tea.
items.alt: It has a spout, a handle and a lid, sits on the stove or an electric base, and British homes switch it on many times a day.

items.name: hammer
items.description: A tool with a heavy metal head on a handle for pounding nails
items.clue: It has a heavy metal head on a handle and you swing it to bang nails into wood.
items.alt: Carpenters keep one on their belt, its back end has a claw for pulling things out, and a judge's wooden version is called a gavel.

items.name: screwdriver
items.description: A hand tool with a narrow tip for turning screws
items.clue: A handle with a long metal shaft and a flat or cross-shaped tip that you twist to tighten or loosen small fasteners.
items.alt: Phillips and flat-head are the two common kinds, and you need one to open the battery cover on a kid's gadget.

items.name: saw
items.description: A tool with a toothed metal blade for cutting through wood
items.clue: A flat metal blade with a row of sharp teeth that you push back and forth to cut through wood.
items.alt: Carpenters cut planks with it, lumberjacks use a big motorized chain version on trees, and magicians pretend to cut a lady in half with one.

items.name: wrench
items.description: A metal hand tool that grips and turns nuts and bolts
items.clue: A metal hand gadget with jaws at the end that grips and turns nuts and bolts.
items.alt: Plumbers use a big adjustable one to tighten pipes, and mechanics keep a set of them in different sizes in their garage.

items.name: shovel
items.description: A long-handled tool with a broad scoop blade for digging dirt
items.clue: A long handle with a wide, scooped metal blade at the end, used for digging holes in the dirt.
items.alt: You clear snow off the driveway with it in winter, and gardeners push it into the ground with their foot.

items.name: rake
items.description: A long-handled garden tool with teeth for gathering leaves
items.clue: A long handle with a row of metal or plastic prongs at the end, used to gather fallen leaves into piles.
items.alt: Gardeners smooth soil with it, and in cartoons someone steps on its teeth and the handle smacks them in the face.

items.name: axe
items.description: A tool with a heavy sharp blade on a handle for chopping wood
items.clue: A heavy wedge-shaped blade on a long wooden handle that you swing to chop firewood or cut down trees.
items.alt: Lumberjacks and firefighters carry one, and you split logs with it at a campsite.

items.name: ladder
items.description: A tall frame with rungs or steps for climbing up high
items.clue: Two long side rails joined by evenly spaced rungs that you climb to reach high spots like a roof.
items.alt: Painters lean it against a wall, a folding step version helps you change a ceiling bulb, and walking under one is said to be unlucky.

items.name: needle
items.description: A thin sharp steel pin with an eye for sewing with thread
items.clue: A very thin, sharp sliver of steel with a tiny eye at one end that you thread to sew cloth.
items.alt: Nurses use a hollow one to give injections, and finding one in a haystack is famously hard.

items.name: nail
items.description: A thin pointed metal spike hammered into wood to fasten things
items.clue: A thin, pointed metal spike with a flat head that you bang into wood with a hammer.
items.alt: Carpenters buy them by the box to join boards, and you might hang a picture on one stuck in the wall.

items.name: lawn mower
items.description: A wheeled machine with spinning blades for cutting grass in a yard
items.clue: A machine with a spinning blade underneath that you push across the grass to cut it short.
items.alt: It roars on Saturday mornings in the suburbs, runs on gasoline or electricity, and has a bag at the back that collects clippings.

items.name: magnet
items.description: A piece of metal that attracts iron and sticks to refrigerators
items.clue: A piece of metal that pulls iron and steel toward it and sticks to the fridge without glue.
items.alt: It has a north and a south pole, opposite ends attract while like ends push away, and a compass needle is one.

items.name: paintbrush
items.description: A handle with soft bristles for spreading paint on surfaces or canvas
items.clue: A wooden handle with soft bristles at the tip that artists dip in color to make pictures on canvas.
items.alt: Decorators use a wide one to coat walls and fences, and you rinse it in a jar of water after doing watercolors.

items.name: pencil
items.description: A wooden writing stick with erasable graphite lead, sharpened to a point
items.clue: A thin wooden stick with graphite inside that you sharpen to a point and use to write or draw.
items.alt: It's often yellow with a pink eraser on the end, and you fill in multiple-choice tests with a No. 2 one.

items.name: pen
items.description: A writing tool that draws lines with ink, usually not erasable
items.clue: A slim stick filled with ink that you click or uncap to write your signature on paper.
