items.alt: Ballpoint, gel and fountain are common kinds, and it's said to be mightier than the sword.

items.name: crayon
items.description: A colored wax stick children use for drawing and coloring pictures
items.clue: A colored wax stick that young children use to draw and fill in coloring books.
items.alt: They come in boxes of 8, 24 or 64, some boxes have a built-in sharpener, and kids often snap them in half.

items.name: eraser
items.description: A small rubber block that rubs away pencil marks
items.clue: A small soft pink or white block you rub on paper to remove pencil mistakes.
items.alt: It often sits on the end of a pencil, wears down as you use it, and leaves little crumbs on your homework.

items.name: ruler
items.description: A flat straight strip marked in inches or centimeters for measuring length
items.clue: A flat, straight strip of wood, plastic or metal marked in inches or centimeters, used to measure and draw straight lines.
items.alt: It's usually 12 inches or 30 centimeters long, and old-fashioned teachers rapped knuckles with it.

items.name: scissors
items.description: A cutting tool with two crossing blades and finger loops for paper
items.clue: Two sharp blades joined in the middle with finger holes on the handles, used to cut paper and fabric.
items.alt: You're told never to run with them, kids use round-tipped safety ones for crafts, and they beat paper in a famous hand game.

items.name: stapler
items.description: A desk tool that pushes metal staples to fasten papers together
items.clue: A desk gadget you press down on to punch a small bent wire through sheets of paper and hold them together.
items.alt: It jams sometimes, you refill it with a strip of thin wire clips, and a famous red one appears in the movie Office Space.

items.name: glue
items.description: A sticky liquid or paste that holds things together when dry
items.clue: A sticky liquid or paste that you use to stick paper, wood or broken pieces together.
items.alt: Kids use a white bottle or a stick of it for craft projects, and super-strong kinds can bond your fingers together by accident.

items.name: book
items.description: Bound printed pages with a cover, containing a story or information to read
items.clue: Many printed pages bound together inside a cover, which you read to learn something or enjoy a story.
items.alt: Libraries lend them out, they have chapters and an author's name on the spine, and you might bring one to bed or on vacation.

items.name: map
items.description: A flat drawing of an area showing roads, places and directions
items.clue: A flat drawing of an area showing roads, cities, rivers and borders so you can find your way.
items.alt: Explorers unfold paper ones, there's usually a compass rose and a legend in the corner, and treasure hunters mark an X on one.

items.name: shirt
items.description: A top garment with sleeves and often buttons, worn on the upper body
items.clue: You wear it on your upper body; it has sleeves and often buttons down the front and a collar.
items.alt: Office workers tuck a crisp white one into their trousers, and a T-shaped cotton kind is printed with logos and slogans.

items.name: pants
items.description: A garment covering each leg separately from the waist to the ankles
items.clue: You wear them on your lower body, with two legs that go down to your ankles, a waistband and pockets.
items.alt: Jeans and khakis are common kinds, you put them on one leg at a time, and you might need a belt to hold them up.

items.name: dress
items.description: A one-piece garment with a skirt, covering the body and legs
items.clue: A one-piece garment with a top and skirt joined together, often worn by women and girls to parties or weddings.
items.alt: A bride wears a long white one, and a little black one is a classic for evening events.

items.name: coat
items.description: A heavy outer garment worn over clothes to stay warm outdoors
items.clue: A warm outer layer with long sleeves and buttons or a zipper that you wear outside in cold weather.
items.alt: You hang it on a hook by the front door, winter ones are puffy or wool, and a waterproof one keeps you dry in a storm.

items.name: sweater
items.description: A warm knitted top with long sleeves, pulled on over the head
items.clue: A warm knitted top with long sleeves, usually made of wool, that you pull on over your head.
items.alt: Grandmas sometimes knit an ugly one with reindeer on it for the holidays, and it can shrink if washed hot.

items.name: hat
items.description: A covering worn on top of the head, often with a brim
items.clue: You wear it on top of your head to keep off the sun or cold, and it can have a brim.
items.alt: Cowboys, chefs and wizards each wear a different style, and magicians pull rabbits out of a tall black one.

items.name: shoe
items.description: Footwear with a sturdy sole, worn on the foot for walking
items.clue: You wear one on each foot to protect it when walking; it has a sole and often laces.
items.alt: Cinderella left a glass one behind at the ball, and you buy them by size and tie their strings in a bow.

items.name: sock
items.description: A soft knitted fabric covering worn on the foot inside a shoe
items.clue: A soft knitted tube of cotton or wool that you pull over your foot before putting on your shoes.
items.alt: They always seem to go missing in the laundry, they come in pairs, and kids hang a big one by the fireplace at Christmas.

items.name: glove
items.description: A covering for the hand with separate fingers, worn for warmth
items.clue: You wear it on your hand to keep it warm, with a separate part for each finger.
items.alt: Doctors snap on thin latex ones, baseball players catch with a leather one, and boxers wear padded ones.

items.name: scarf
items.description: A long strip of cloth wrapped around the neck for warmth
items.clue: A long strip of soft knitted or woven fabric that you wrap around your neck to stay warm.
items.alt: Football fans wave ones in their team colors, and some women knot a silk one over their hair.

items.name: belt
items.description: A strap with a buckle worn around the waist to hold pants up
items.clue: A strip of leather with a buckle that goes through the loops of your pants to hold them up.
items.alt: Karate students earn colored ones as they advance, and wrestling champions win a big gold one.

items.name: tie
items.description: A long narrow cloth strip knotted at the collar of a dress shirt
items.clue: A long, narrow strip of silk that men knot around their neck under a shirt collar for formal occasions.
items.alt: Businessmen wear it with a suit, it's a common Father's Day gift, and the bow version is shaped like a butterfly.

items.name: glasses
items.description: Clear lenses in a frame worn over the eyes to see better
items.clue: A frame with two lenses that sits on your nose and ears to help you see clearly.
items.alt: An optician fits you for them after an eye test, and you clean their lenses with a soft cloth when they get smudged.

items.name: sunglasses
items.description: Dark tinted lenses in a frame worn to shade eyes from sunlight
items.clue: Dark tinted lenses in a frame that you wear on a bright day to protect your eyes from the glare.
items.alt: People wear them at the beach and while driving into the late afternoon, and celebrities hide behind big ones.

items.name: watch
items.description: A small timepiece worn on a strap around the wrist
items.clue: A small timepiece with a strap that you wear on your wrist to check the hour.
items.alt: It has a face and a buckle band, some count your steps and heart rate, and you glance at it when you're late.

items.name: ring
items.description: A small circular band of metal worn on a finger
items.clue: A small band of gold or silver worn around your finger, sometimes set with a diamond.
items.alt: Couples exchange them at a wedding, and someone kneels down to offer one when proposing marriage.

items.name: necklace
items.description: A chain or string of beads worn around the neck as jewelry
items.clue: A chain or string of beads or pearls worn around your throat as jewelry, often with a pendant hanging at the front.
items.alt: It fastens with a tiny clasp at the back, and a locket holding a photo can hang from it on your chest.

items.name: earring
items.description: A small piece of jewelry worn on the earlobe
items.clue: A small piece of jewelry worn through a pierced lobe on the side of your head, like a stud or a hoop.
items.alt: They usually come in pairs, pirates are pictured with a gold hoop one, and people get them after a piercing at the mall.

items.name: umbrella
items.description: A folding canopy on a handle held overhead to keep off rain
items.clue: A folding canopy of waterproof fabric on a handle that you open over your head to stay dry in the rain.
items.alt: It has a curved handle and metal spokes, it's bad luck to open one indoors, and Mary Poppins floated down holding one.

items.name: wallet
items.description: A small flat folding case for carrying money and cards in a pocket
items.clue: A small folding leather case you keep in your pocket to hold cash, cards and your ID.
items.alt: If you lose it you have to cancel your credit cards, and it often holds family photos and receipts.

items.name: helmet
items.description: A hard protective hat that guards the head from injury
items.clue: A hard, padded shell you wear on your head to protect it when riding a bike or playing football.
items.alt: Astronauts, soldiers, knights and construction workers each wear a different kind, and it straps under your chin.

items.name: backpack
items.description: A bag with two shoulder straps carried on the back
items.clue: A bag with two shoulder straps that students carry to class with books and lunch inside.
items.alt: Hikers carry a big one with water and supplies on trails, and it has zippered pockets and a padded section for a laptop.

items.name: ball
items.description: A round bouncy object thrown, kicked or caught in games
items.clue: A round, bouncy sphere that kids throw, kick and catch, and that soccer and tennis can't be played without.
items.alt: Dogs love to fetch one, it can be inflated with a pump, and it rolls away down the hill if you drop it.

items.name: doll
items.description: A small toy figure shaped like a person or baby
items.clue: A small figure shaped like a baby or a person that children dress up, comb and pretend to care for.
items.alt: Some have eyes that close when laid down, Russian nesting ones fit inside each other, and kids host tea parties for them.

items.name: teddy bear
items.description: A soft stuffed toy bear that children cuddle
items.clue: A soft, stuffed animal with fuzzy brown fur, button eyes and round ears that children cuddle at bedtime.
items.alt: It's named after President Theodore Roosevelt, and Winnie the Pooh is the most famous one.

items.name: kite
items.description: A light frame covered in fabric flown in the wind on a string
items.clue: A light frame covered in paper or nylon that you fly high in the wind on a long string.
items.alt: You run across a windy beach to launch it, it has a long tail with bows, and Benjamin Franklin famously tested lightning with one.

items.name: puzzle
items.description: A picture cut into interlocking pieces that you fit back together
items.clue: Hundreds of oddly shaped cardboard pieces that you fit together on a table to make a picture.
items.alt: You start with the edge pieces, there's always one missing at the end, and crossword and Rubik's cube kinds are brain teasers too.

items.name: balloon
items.description: A thin rubber bag inflated with air or helium that floats
items.clue: A thin rubber bag that you blow up with air or helium so it floats, often tied with a string at birthday parties.
items.alt: It pops with a loud bang if you poke it with a pin, and you can rub it on your hair to make static.

items.name: yo-yo
items.description: A toy of two joined discs that spins up and down a string
items.clue: Two round discs joined by an axle with a string wound around it that you make spin down and climb back up to your hand.
items.alt: Kids do tricks with it like walking the dog and rocking the baby, and its string loops around your finger.

items.name: skateboard
items.description: A narrow board on four small wheels ridden by standing and pushing
items.clue: A narrow wooden deck on four small wheels that you stand on and push along with one foot, doing tricks like ollies.
items.alt: Teens ride it on ramps and half-pipes at the park, and it became an Olympic event in 2021.

items.name: jump rope
items.description: A rope swung over the head and under the feet while jumping
items.clue: A long cord with handles at each end that you swing over your head and hop over again and again.
items.alt: Boxers use it to train their footwork, and kids chant rhymes at recess while two friends turn it for a third to skip.

items.name: dice
items.description: Small cubes with one to six dots, rolled in board games
items.clue: Small cubes with one to six dots on their sides that you roll to get a random number in board pastimes.
items.alt: Gamblers throw a pair of them on the craps table in casinos, and opposite faces always add up to seven.

items.name: playing card
items.description: A thin printed card with a suit and number from a deck of fifty-two
items.clue: One of 52 flat rectangles in a deck, marked with hearts, diamonds, clubs or spades and a number or a face.
items.alt: You shuffle and deal them for poker or solitaire, and magicians ask you to pick one and remember it.

items.name: chess
items.description: A strategy board game with kings, queens and pawns on a checkered board
items.clue: A board pastime with kings, queens, bishops, knights, rooks and pawns on a checkered 8 by 8 board.
items.alt: Two players try to checkmate each other, and grandmasters compete in tournaments using a timer clock.

items.name: marble
items.description: A small glass ball rolled and flicked in children's games
items.clue: A small glass ball with colorful swirls inside that kids roll and flick to knock others out of a circle.
items.alt: Children collect them in little pouches, big ones are called shooters, and losing them means you've gone a bit crazy.

items.name: rubber duck
items.description: A small yellow squeaky toy duck that floats in the bathtub
items.clue: A small yellow squeaky bath companion shaped like a waterbird with an orange beak that floats in the tub.
items.alt: Toddlers squeeze it at bath time, programmers explain bugs to it at their desk, and it bobs on the water with a little quack.

items.name: frisbee
items.description: A flat plastic flying disc thrown spinning between players
items.clue: A flat plastic disc that you throw with a flick of the wrist so it glides through the air for a friend or dog to catch.
items.alt: People toss it on the beach or in the park, and ultimate is a team version played with it.

items.name: baseball bat
items.description: A long rounded wooden or metal club for hitting a baseball
items.clue: A long, smooth wooden or aluminum club that a hitter swings to send a pitch flying in America's pastime.
items.alt: It's thick at the end and narrow at the handle, and players tap it on home plate before taking a swing.

items.name: tennis racket
items.description: An oval frame with tight strings on a handle for hitting tennis balls
items.clue: An oval frame strung with a tight net of strings on a handle, used to hit a fuzzy yellow ball over a net.
items.alt: Players at Wimbledon swing it in forehand and backhand strokes, and its strings need replacing when they snap.

items.name: sled
items.description: A low board or seat on runners for sliding down snowy hills
items.clue: You sit or lie on it and slide down a snowy hill at high speed in winter.
items.alt: Santa's is pulled by reindeer, kids drag a plastic one back up the slope by a rope, and teams of dogs pull them across the Arctic.

items.name: trampoline
items.description: A stretchy fabric mat on springs in a frame for bouncing high
items.clue: A large springy mat stretched across a metal frame that you bounce high on in the back garden.
items.alt: Gymnasts flip and twist on it, and families put safety netting around it so kids don't fly off the edge.

items.name: hula hoop
items.description: A large plastic ring spun around the waist by swinging the hips
items.clue: A big plastic ring that you spin around your waist by wiggling your hips to keep it from falling.
items.alt: It was a huge craze in the 1950s, and performers twirl several at once around their arms, neck and legs.

items.name: piano
items.description: A large keyboard instrument with black and white keys striking strings
items.clue: It has 88 black and white keys that you press to play music, and it's large enough to fill a corner of a room.
items.alt: Beethoven and Mozart composed for it, it has pedals at the bottom, and a grand one is played at concerts.

items.name: guitar
items.description: A stringed instrument with a long neck and six strings, strummed or plucked
items.clue: It has six strings stretched over a wooden body and a long neck, and you strum or pluck it.
items.alt: Rock stars play electric ones through amplifiers, and people sing around a campfire while someone plays an acoustic one.

items.name: drum
items.description: A percussion instrument with stretched skin, hit with sticks or hands
items.clue: A hollow cylinder with skin or plastic stretched tightly over the top that you hit with sticks to keep the beat.
items.alt: Marching bands have a big bass one, and a full kit has snares, toms and cymbals played at the back of a rock band.

items.name: violin
items.description: A small wooden stringed instrument held under the chin and played with a bow
items.clue: A small wooden thing with four strings, tucked under the chin and played by drawing a horsehair bow across it.
items.alt: It's the smallest of the orchestra's string family, with an hourglass body and f-shaped holes, and Stradivarius made famous ones.

items.name: trumpet
items.description: A brass wind instrument with three valves and a flared bell
items.clue: A shiny brass horn with three valves that you blow into and press to play loud, bright notes.
items.alt: It's heard in jazz clubs and military bugle calls, and Louis Armstrong was its most famous player.

items.name: flute
items.description: A slender metal woodwind tube held sideways and played by blowing across a hole
items.clue: A long, thin silver tube with keys that you hold sideways and blow across a hole to play high notes.
items.alt: It sits in the woodwind section of an orchestra even though it's made of metal, and the Pied Piper's pipe is a relative.

items.name: saxophone
items.description: A curved brass woodwind with a reed and keys, popular in jazz
items.clue: A curved brass horn shaped like a J with a reed mouthpiece, famous for its smooth sound in jazz.
items.alt: Bill Clinton played one on late-night TV, and it comes in alto, tenor and baritone sizes for rock and soul solos.

items.name: harp
items.description: A large upright triangular frame of many strings plucked with the fingers
items.clue: A tall triangular frame with dozens of strings that you pluck with your fingers while sitting beside it.
items.alt: Angels are often pictured playing one on clouds, and it's a national symbol of Ireland.

items.name: xylophone
items.description: A percussion instrument of wooden bars struck with mallets
items.clue: A row of wooden bars of different lengths that you hit with small mallets to make ringing notes.
items.alt: It's often on alphabet posters for the letter X, and toddlers get colorful little versions that go plink from low to high.

items.name: accordion
items.description: A squeezebox instrument with bellows and a keyboard, pushed and pulled
items.clue: You squeeze and pull its folding bellows in and out while pressing keys or buttons, and it's strapped to your chest.
items.alt: It's heard in polkas, French cafe music and Mexican norteno bands, and it wheezes with a reedy sound.

items.name: tambourine
items.description: A small hand drum with jingling metal discs around its rim, shaken
items.clue: A small round frame with jingling metal discs around the edge that you shake or tap with your hand.
items.alt: Backup singers rattle it in time to the song, and it may have a skin stretched across one side like a little drum.

items.name: bell
items.description: A hollow metal cup that rings when struck by its clapper
items.clue: A hollow metal cup shape that rings when the clapper inside swings against it.
items.alt: Churches hang big ones in their towers, and handheld ones are rung at Christmas by charity collectors.

items.name: house
items.description: A building where a family lives, with bedrooms, kitchen and yard
items.clue: Where a family lives, with a roof, walls, a front door, bedrooms and a kitchen.
items.alt: You might buy one with a mortgage, it has a yard and a chimney, and people call it home sweet home.

items.name: school
items.description: A building with classrooms where children are taught by teachers
items.clue: Children go there on weekdays to learn from teachers in classrooms, with a playground and a cafeteria.
items.alt: It has a principal, lockers and a bell between lessons, and it closes for a few months over summer vacation.

items.name: castle
items.description: A large old fortified stone building with towers and walls, home of kings
items.clue: A huge old stone fortress with towers, thick walls and a moat where kings and queens once lived.
items.alt: Knights defended it with a drawbridge and battlements, and fairy tales lock princesses in its tallest tower.

items.name: church
items.description: A building for Christian worship, often with a steeple and cross
items.clue: A religious hall with a steeple and stained-glass windows where Christians gather to worship on Sundays.
items.alt: Weddings and funerals are held there, a priest or pastor preaches from the pulpit, and its bells ring on the hour.

items.name: hospital
items.description: A building where doctors and nurses treat sick and injured patients
items.clue: Sick and injured people go there to be treated by doctors and nurses and stay in beds on wards.
items.alt: It has an emergency room, operating theaters and a maternity ward where babies are born.

items.name: bridge
items.description: A structure that spans over a river or road so people can cross
items.clue: It stretches over a river or road so cars and people can cross from one side to the other.
items.alt: The Golden Gate in San Francisco is a famous red suspension one, and a troll hides under one in a fairy tale.

items.name: lighthouse
items.description: A tall coastal tower with a bright light guiding ships at night
items.clue: A tall tower on the coast with a powerful lamp at the top that flashes to warn ships away from rocks at night.
items.alt: It's often painted with red and white stripes, a keeper used to live inside it, and its beam sweeps across the sea in the dark.

items.name: skyscraper
items.description: A very tall city building with many floors of offices
items.clue: An extremely tall city tower with dozens or hundreds of floors of offices, reached by fast elevators.
items.alt: New York and Dubai are famous for them, and the Burj Khalifa is the tallest one in the world at over 800 meters.

items.name: tent
items.description: A portable fabric shelter on poles, set up for camping outdoors
items.clue: A fabric shelter held up by poles and pegs that you sleep in when you go camping.
items.alt: You pitch it at a campsite, zip the door shut against bugs, and circuses perform under a giant striped one.

items.name: igloo
items.description: A dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of packed snow
items.clue: A dome-shaped shelter made of blocks of packed snow, traditionally built by Inuit people in the Arctic.
items.alt: It has a low tunnel entrance and is surprisingly warm inside despite being built from frozen blocks.

items.name: pyramid
items.description: A huge ancient stone structure with four triangular sides meeting at a point
items.clue: A huge ancient stone monument with a square base and four triangular sides meeting at a point, found in Egypt.
items.alt: Pharaohs were buried inside them with treasure, and the Great one at Giza is one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

items.name: barn
items.description: A large farm building for storing hay and housing animals
items.clue: A large red wooden farm shed where cows, horses and hay are kept.
items.alt: It has big double doors and a hayloft, and country folk hold square dances in them.

items.name: library
items.description: A building full of books that people borrow and read quietly
items.clue: A quiet hall full of shelves of books that you can borrow for free with a card.
items.alt: You have to whisper there, return what you borrowed by the due date, and it has computers and story time for kids.

items.name: airport
items.description: A place with runways and terminals where airplanes take off and land
items.clue: Where you go to catch a flight, with runways, terminals, security lines and baggage claim.
items.alt: You check in your suitcase there, wait at a gate, and watch jets take off through big windows.

items.name: playground
items.description: An outdoor area with swings, slides and climbing equipment for children
items.clue: An outdoor area in a park with swings, slides, monkey bars and a sandbox for children.
items.alt: Kids run around there at recess, climbing jungle gyms and going down the twisty slide while parents watch from benches.

items.name: museum
items.description: A building displaying art, history or science exhibits for visitors
items.clue: A hall where you look at old artifacts, art, dinosaur skeletons and exhibits behind glass.
items.alt: Visitors walk quietly through its galleries, and the Louvre in Paris with the Mona Lisa is a famous one.

items.name: stadium
items.description: A huge arena with tiers of seats around a field for sports
items.clue: A huge open-air arena with thousands of seats around a field where crowds watch football or concerts.
items.alt: Fans do the wave in its stands, buy hot dogs there, and it has floodlights for night matches.

items.name: sun
items.description: The bright hot star at the center of our solar system, giving daylight
items.clue: The big bright yellow ball in the daytime sky that gives us light and warmth.
items.alt: It's the star at the center of our solar system, rises in the east and sets in the west, and you can get burned if you stay out too long.

items.name: moon
items.description: Earth's rocky natural satellite that orbits it and shines at night
items.clue: It glows white in the night sky, changes from a thin crescent to a full circle each month, and orbits the Earth.
items.alt: Neil Armstrong walked on it in 1969, it pulls the ocean tides, and it's covered in gray craters.

items.name: star
items.description: A distant burning ball of gas seen twinkling in the night sky
items.clue: One of the tiny twinkling points of light you see scattered across the night sky.
items.alt: It's a giant ball of glowing hot gas very far away, our sun is one, and sailors navigated by the northern one called Polaris.

items.name: planet
items.description: A large world orbiting the sun, like Mars, Jupiter or Saturn
items.clue: A huge round world that orbits the sun, like Mars, Jupiter or Saturn.
items.alt: Our solar system has eight of them, and Pluto was demoted from the list in 2006.

items.name: earth
items.description: Our home planet, the third from the sun, with oceans and land
items.clue: The third world from the sun, the blue-and-green home of every human, mostly covered in ocean.
items.alt: Astronauts photographed it as a blue marble from the moon, and it spins once every 24 hours.

items.name: rainbow
items.description: An arc of colored bands in the sky after rain
items.clue: A colorful arc across the sky after a shower, when sunlight passes through water droplets.
items.alt: It has seven colors from red to violet, and legend says a pot of gold waits at its end.

items.name: cloud
items.description: A white or gray mass of water droplets floating in the sky
items.clue: A white or gray fluffy shape floating high in the sky, made of tiny water droplets.
items.alt: Dark ones bring storms, kids find animal shapes in them, and planes fly through them causing bumps.

items.name: snow
items.description: Soft white ice flakes that fall from the sky in cold weather
items.clue: Cold white flakes that fall from the sky in winter and cover the ground so you can build a man with a carrot nose.
items.alt: Kids hope for a day off from class when it piles up, and each six-sided crystal flake is said to be unique.

items.name: rain
items.description: Drops of water falling from clouds in the sky
items.clue: Drops of water falling from gray clouds that make you open an umbrella and leave puddles on the ground.
items.alt: Plants need it to grow, it patters on the roof during a storm, and Seattle and London are famous for lots of it.

items.name: lightning
items.description: A bright electric flash in the sky during a thunderstorm
items.clue: A sudden jagged bolt of electricity that flashes from the clouds during a storm, followed by thunder.
items.alt: It's hotter than the sun's surface, and you count the seconds before the boom to tell how far away it struck.

items.name: tornado
items.description: A violent spinning funnel of wind reaching down from a storm cloud
items.clue: A violent spinning funnel of wind that touches down from a storm and destroys houses in its path.
items.alt: It's common in Kansas and Oklahoma, and in The Wizard of Oz one carries Dorothy's house away.

items.name: volcano
items.description: A mountain that erupts with lava, ash and smoke from inside the earth
items.clue: A mountain that erupts with red-hot lava, ash and smoke from a crater at the top.
items.alt: Vesuvius buried Pompeii in 79 AD, Hawaii's islands were built by them, and kids make baking-soda models of one that fizz over.

items.name: mountain
items.description: A very tall natural rise of land with a steep rocky peak
items.clue: A huge, tall landform rising high above the surrounding land, with steep rocky slopes and often a snowy peak.
items.alt: Climbers need ropes and oxygen to reach the summit of the tallest one, Everest, and people ski down them in winter.

items.name: river
items.description: A long flowing stream of fresh water running across land to the sea
items.clue: A long stream of fresh water that flows across the land into the sea, with banks on both sides.
items.alt: The Nile and the Amazon are the longest, people fish and paddle canoes on it, and bridges cross it in cities.

items.name: ocean
items.description: A vast body of salty water covering most of the earth
items.clue: The huge body of salty water that covers most of the Earth, with waves, whales and coral reefs.
items.alt: The Pacific is the biggest one, ships take weeks to cross it, and its deepest point is the Mariana Trench.

items.name: waterfall
items.description: Water falling steeply over a cliff or rocky ledge in a river
items.clue: A spot where a river drops over a cliff edge, crashing down onto rocks below with mist and spray.
items.alt: Niagara on the US-Canada border and Victoria in Africa are famous ones, and daredevils have gone over in barrels.

items.name: island
items.description: A piece of land completely surrounded by water
items.clue: An area of ground completely surrounded by sea, like Hawaii, Jamaica or Madagascar.
items.alt: Castaways get stranded on an uninhabited one with palm trees, and you reach it by boat or ferry.

items.name: desert
items.description: A dry, hot sandy region with very little rain or plants
items.clue: A vast dry area of sand dunes and rocks where it hardly ever rains, like the Sahara.
items.alt: Camels cross it, cacti grow there, and it's scorching by day but can be freezing at night.

items.name: cave
items.description: A dark hollow space underground or inside a rocky hillside
items.clue: A dark hollow opening in the side of a hill or cliff that goes deep underground.
items.alt: Bats hang from its ceiling, stalactites drip from above, and early humans painted animals on its walls.

items.name: beach
items.description: A sandy or pebbly shore where land meets the sea
items.clue: A sandy strip along the edge of the sea where people sunbathe, swim and build sandcastles.
items.alt: You lay out a towel there, collect seashells, and the waves wash up on the shore at high tide.

items.name: fire
items.description: Hot glowing flames and smoke from something burning
items.clue: Hot orange flames and smoke that come from burning wood, giving off heat and light.
items.alt: Early humans learned to make it by rubbing sticks, you sit around one at camp roasting marshmallows, and crews with hoses put it out.

items.name: diamond
items.description: A clear, extremely hard sparkling gem made of carbon
items.clue: The hardest natural substance, a clear sparkling stone often set in engagement rings.
items.alt: It's made of pure carbon pressed deep underground, it's measured in carats, and it's said to be a girl's best friend.

items.name: gold
items.description: A shiny yellow precious metal used for jewelry and coins
items.clue: A shiny yellow precious element used for jewelry, coins and Olympic first-place medals.
items.alt: Prospectors panned rivers for it in the 1849 rush to California, and its chemical symbol is Au.

items.name: silver
items.description: A shiny white-gray precious metal used for jewelry, coins and silverware
items.clue: A shiny grayish-white precious element used for jewelry, cutlery and second-place medals.
items.alt: Its chemical symbol is Ag, it tarnishes black if not polished, and legends say bullets made of it can kill werewolves.

items.name: iron
items.description: A strong gray metal that rusts, used to make steel
items.clue: A strong gray element dug from ore that rusts when wet and is made into steel for skyscrapers and bridges.
items.alt: Its chemical symbol is Fe, magnets attract it, and your blood needs it, which is why spinach is said to be good for you.

items.name: rock
items.description: A hard solid chunk of natural stone from the ground
items.clue: A hard, heavy chunk of the earth's crust that you find lying on the ground, on beaches and in mountains.
items.alt: Geologists sort it into igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic types, and kids skip flat ones across a pond.

items.name: sand
items.description: Tiny loose grains of crushed rock found on beaches and deserts
items.clue: Tiny grains of crushed rock and shell that cover beaches and deserts.
items.alt: It trickles through an hourglass, gets into your shoes and swimsuit, and is melted down to make glass.

items.name: glass
items.description: A hard clear brittle material made from melted sand, used in windows
items.clue: A hard, clear, brittle substance used for windows, bottles and drinking tumblers that shatters when dropped.
items.alt: It's made by melting sand at very high heat, artisans blow it into shapes, and you recycle it in a separate bin.

items.name: plastic
items.description: A light, moldable man-made material from oil, used for bottles and toys
items.clue: A light, man-made substance made from petroleum that can be molded into bottles, bags, toys and containers.
items.alt: It takes hundreds of years to break down, it pollutes the oceans, and you're asked to recycle it by the number stamped on the bottom.

items.name: ice
items.description: Frozen solid water, cold, hard and slippery
items.clue: Water frozen solid into a cold, slippery, see-through substance that you put in drinks.
items.alt: Skaters glide on it at the rink, it melts at 0 degrees Celsius, and it floats in a glass of soda.

items.name: water
items.description: A clear tasteless liquid that people drink and that fills rivers
items.clue: A clear liquid with no taste or smell that you drink every day, and it falls as rain and fills rivers.
items.alt: Its chemical formula is H2O, it boils at 100 degrees Celsius, and people are told to drink about eight glasses of it a day.

items.name: salt
items.description: White crystals mined or taken from seawater, used to season food
items.clue: White crystals that you shake onto food to make it taste better, often kept beside the pepper.
items.alt: It's sodium chloride, it's scattered on icy roads in winter, and sea water is full of it.

items.name: coal
items.description: A black rock dug from mines and burned as fuel
items.clue: A black, dusty rock that is mined from underground and burned to make heat and electricity.
items.alt: Naughty children supposedly get a lump of it in their stocking at Christmas, and steam trains burned it in their engines.

items.name: ruby
items.description: A red precious gemstone used in jewelry
items.clue: A precious deep-red stone that sparkles in rings and crowns.
items.alt: It's a red form of the mineral corundum, it's the birthstone for July, and Dorothy's magic slippers were named after it.

items.name: brick
items.description: A rectangular block of baked clay used to build walls
items.clue: A hard red rectangular block of baked clay that is stacked with mortar to build walls and houses.
items.alt: The third little pig's sturdy home was made of these, and masons lay them in neat rows.

items.name: concrete
items.description: A gray building material of cement, sand and gravel that hardens
items.clue: A gray mixture of cement, sand, gravel and water that is poured wet and hardens into sidewalks and foundations.
items.alt: Trucks with spinning drums deliver it to job sites, and kids sometimes press their handprints into it before it sets.
